Moving-holiday window regressors

Source: R/window.R
holiday_window.Rd

Computes, for every period of a monthly or quarterly series, the share of each holiday window `[date + window[1], date + window[2]]` (in days) that falls in that period: wj,t=∣Wj∩Pt∣/∣Wj∣,w_{j,t} = |W_j \cap P_t| / |W_j|,wj,t​=∣Wj​∩Pt​∣/∣Wj​∣, where WjW_jWj​ is the window around occurrence jjj and PtP_tPt​ the set of days of period ttt.

Usage

holiday_window(dates, window = c(0, 0), y, h = 0, per_event = FALSE)

Arguments

dates

`Date` vector of holiday occurrences.

window

Numeric `c(pre, post)` in days relative to each date, e.g. `c(-3, 7)` for three days before to seven days after. `c(0, 0)` reproduces the usual dummy for the period containing the holiday.

y

A `ts` object (frequency 12 or 4) defining start and length.

h

Number of future periods to append.

per_event

If `TRUE`, one column per occurrence; otherwise their sum (one column named `holiday`).

Value

A `ts` matrix with `length(y) + h` rows.

Examples

w <- holiday_window(holiday_dates("idul_adha"), c(-3, 7), sapi)
# Eid al-Adha on 31 July 2020: most of the window falls in August
window(w, start = c(2020, 6), end = c(2020, 9))
#>            Jun       Jul       Aug       Sep
#> 2020 0.0000000 0.3636364 0.6363636 0.0000000
